Objective: Determine whether the organization is ready to run the copilot company-wide, name who owns each unresolved piece of work and their first concrete action, and surface the business-case and ownership gaps that make "readiness" currently unanswerable — before any go-live date is discussed.

Body: I cannot certify readiness. Nobody has asked the people doing the work whether they can do it the new way, and the resistance we do have is being treated as noise, not evidence.

ADKAR read: the stall is at **Desire**, not Knowledge — training will not fix it. Resistance likely reflects lost discretion to override a wrong diagnosis safely, and possibly fear that the payback case assumes their own jobs. A training calendar now produces hollow completion numbers.

**Gates, owners, first action:**
1. *Capability* — Owner: Compliance/Model Risk Lead. First action (this week): determine AI Act high-risk classification for safety-critical repair guidance; this determines conformity obligations before the golden dataset is validated, not after. Golden dataset validation follows, not concurrently.
2. *Role clarity* — Owner: Field Operations Process Lead. First action (3 weeks): draw the disputed-diagnosis process — who adjudicates, how overrides are recorded. Highest-leverage gap; gates curriculum design.
3. *Capacity* — Owner: Field Ops Director. First action: staff a resource plan for the currently unresourced workstream and name manager backfill during transition; unresourced managers become the failure point at month four.
4. *Architecture/integration* — Owner: Engineering/Architecture Lead. First action (3 weeks): decide model/architecture and produce an integration blueprint to the FSM system, scoped against the escalation workflow's requirements from gate 2, not independently of them.
5. *Support cover* — Owner: Field Ops Process Lead (with Engineering). First action: define real-time field escalation route.

**Named business owner — currently missing.** No single person is accountable for forcing closure across all five gates. Until named, this plan is a set of recommendations with no enforcement mechanism.

**Role-by-role impact:**
- *Technicians*: lose standing to trust their own judgment unless escalation protects it. Learn: dispute workflow, taught by senior technicians in paired shifts, 4–6 weeks [ASSUMPTION: comparable field rollouts; validate with technicians].
- *Line managers*: absorb change twice, no backfill named — see gate 3.
- *Dispatchers/FSM admins*: impact unscoped. First action: FSM system owner joins the architecture kickoff (gate 4) so their workflow changes get scoped in the same window as everyone else's, not left implicit.

**Curriculum**: cannot finalize until gates 2 and 4 close — sequence Awareness comms now, dispute training once process exists, paired practice, reinforcement.

**Reinforcement (90 days post-launch):** override/dispute rate by cohort, denominator = technicians using tool on live jobs, not logins. Weekly manager check-ins, escalation SLA tracking, quarterly bias-audit refresh.

Citations:
- Prosci ADKAR Model: https://www.prosci.com/methodology/adkar
- EU AI Act high-risk classification: https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/high-level-summary/

Risks: The rollout date appears set before readiness work existed — say this to the sponsor first. No business owner is named to run the rollout end-to-end; without one, nobody can force closure across the five gates, and this plan has no enforcement mechanism. The pilot's payback case has not been checked for whether it assumes reduced headcount — if it does, that is the real driver of technician and manager resistance, not a training gap, and it must be stated to the workforce in plain words, not disguised as productivity. Least-ready roles: technicians (no safe way to disagree with the system) and line managers (double burden, unresourced). Five of five readiness gates unevidenced; AI Act classification undetermined, which could force redesign after training is built if missed.

Next Steps: Sponsor names a single accountable business owner this week — without this, no other step proceeds on schedule. I run the first readiness conversation within two weeks with field technicians directly, on where and why they override the pilot tool. Process Lead drafts the escalation workflow in 3 weeks. Compliance Lead determines AI Act classification in 1 week, before golden-dataset work proceeds. Architecture Lead, with the FSM system owner, decides architecture and integration approach in 3 weeks. Someone runs the pilot's business case against actual data now and states plainly whether headcount reduction is assumed. Reconvene in four weeks with evidence against all five gates, not a status update.
